entries.postTitle: Automation vs Batch Creation for Artists

captions.threads:
1/4 I set up a Zapier automation last year that was supposed to handle my content scheduling. Three months later I was getting digest emails I never read, watching posts go out at times nobody I know was actually online, and feeling this weird distance from work that used to feel alive. That's when I realized automation and batch creation are solving different problems wearing the same name.

2/4 Automation wants to remove you from the loop. It's beautiful for things that genuinely don't need your presence, your intuition, your moment-to-moment awareness. But content? Your voice lives in the friction of creation. When you batch create, you're building momentum, finding patterns in your own thinking, staying close enough to course-correct. You're still in conversation with the work.

3/4 The trick isn't choosing one. It's being honest about which parts of your process actually benefit from being hands-off versus which parts need your attention. Maybe you automate your email lists but batch your creative output. Maybe you set up distribution workflows but keep ideation live. The specificity matters more than the ideology.

4/4 What I found is that creators who thrive aren't the ones with the most sophisticated automation. They're the ones who stayed connected to why they make things in the first place. The tools should fade. Your voice shouldn't.

Sit with this one.

entries.postTitle: Outgrowing Old Identities

captions.threads:
nobody warns you that the identity that got you here might be the exact thing holding you back now. i spent years perfecting this version of myself, optimizing for it, building everything around it. then one day it just... didn't fit anymore.

like wearing the same shirt for a decade. it was comfortable. it worked. people knew me in it. but my shoulders changed shape. my chest expanded. the sleeves started pulling weird.

the weird part? shedding it felt like losing something real even though it was always just a costume i put on every morning. there's grief in outgrowing yourself. there's also relief.

if you've ever felt that misalignment where your outsides don't match your insides anymore, where the strategies that built you aren't building you forward, that's not a failure. that's momentum asking for an upgrade.
